newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean stocks close up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: South Korean stocks close up on technical rebound.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Friday in a broad-based technical rebound following recent sharp declines, brokers said.
But they said the market's underlying sentiment remained bearish under pressure from a high level of margin loans.
"The market will continue to drag at least until the margin loans fall below the customer deposits," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
The composite stock index ended 7.26 points higher at a provisional 750.29. Advancers beat decliners 741 to 145.
Brokers said institutional investors stayed away from the market while individuals focused on stocks that posted big losses recently.
Shares of Doosan Group affiliates soared on bargain hunting. The group's shares fell sharply early this week on rumours that the conglomerate faced financial difficulties, brokers said.
Doosan Beverage rose 1,500 won to its daily limit of 26,900 and Doosan Construction gained 500 won to 10,000.
Hanbo Steel closed 120 won higher at 9,500 after touching its upper limit of 9,940 on news that the government was opposed to the construction of an additional steel mill.
